doc.title: Lou Pallo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007

title: Choosing guitar and the Italian family Sunday get-togethers
summary: Pallo drops electronics and airline studies for guitar lessons; his father plays open chords and the family sings and plays mandolin every Sunday.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Not really determined it but I really loved music when I was a kid and I was doing many things. I was of course in high school taking guitar lessons, I was doing electronics, I was going to electronic school, radio and television, and I think — oh airline — something with the airlines. My father says, “You can only do one thing.” So then I went just with the guitar. I stayed with the guitar lessons.
Was yours a musical household that would steer you in that direction?
My father played a little guitar, played in the back yard when they had the get-togethers, he played the open chords, the G and the C and the G7.
Everybody sang. It was a get-together every Sunday and they had mandolin players cause it was an Italian family. Every Sunday. So that’s what made me really want to get into the guitar.
Neat. What kind of songs would they have done?
A lot of, well like “Mexicali Rose” — I don’t know if you have ever heard that song.
Oh you have, okay. A lot of waltzes, polkas, and a few standards, very few standards.
Okay, but not just Italian songs then.
